nodes.description: The root lesion is biallelic loss of DNAJC6, which encodes auxilin, a neuron-selective HSP40/DnaJ co-chaperone. Through its J domain auxilin recruits HSC70 and stimulates its ATPase activity to drive ATP-dependent disassembly of the clathrin coat, so a null or deleterious allele removes the neuron's dedicated clathrin-uncoating activity. The reported juvenile allele produced abnormal transcripts and markedly reduced DNAJC6 mRNA, and a later nonsense allele (p.Cys325*) is predicted to truncate the protein, both consistent with loss of function.

evidence.snippet: Neuronally expressed auxilin and ubiquitously expressed cyclin-G-dependent kinase (GAK) are homologous proteins that act as cochaperones to support the Hsc70-dependent clathrin uncoating of clathrin-coated vesicles.

nodes.description: CRISPR-Cas9-edited human embryonic stem cell midbrain-like organoids carrying DNAJC6 mutations, which reproduce dopaminergic neuron degeneration, alpha-synuclein aggregation and neurodevelopmental defects, and in which the WNT-LMX1A developmental defect was demonstrated.

Dopaminergic agonists and anticholinergics are used alongside levodopa for symptomatic treatment, per GeneReviews; ropinirole was used in a reported juvenile case. Conversely, dopamine antagonists and VMAT2 inhibitors are avoided, as they would aggravate the dopamine deficit; that caution is recorded as a sourced evidence item on the Striatal Dopamine Deficiency and Basal Ganglia Circuit Dysfunction node.
